transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood CSM), Marta Lopez (NovusHealth Lead ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Novus PM), J. Kim (Novus Platform), Renee (Novus Data Privacy)

Summary:
Quick sync to triage model catalog mismatches seen in last pilot run, confirm version pin strategy, and agree on a soft escape (fallback) plan and rollback runbook. Run-through of recent benchmark spikes and dataset-specific regressions.

Topics:
- Catalog differences (v1.3 int8 vs v1.2 fp16)
- Regression examples and golden prompt list
- Soft escape / fallback routing and pinning granularity
- Rollback / emergency cutover checklist and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining on short notice, um we'll do a 40 minute checkin, agenda is catalog triage, pinning, and the soft escape plan, cool?
[00:18] Marta Lopez: yeah sounds good, we saw a handful of odd completions in last week's run and wanted to walk through them, some hallucinationy stuff on long medical instructions which is bad for us
[00:30] Priya Nair: right, we noticed that when you pinned to the int8-quantized v1.3 there were about 8% more token diffs on the long-form guidance prompts versus your previous fp16 v1.2 baseline, may be quantization sensitivity on the decoder head.
[00:48] Samir Patel: 8% is a bit fuzzy for us—what does that actually mean in customer impact? latency went down which is great, cost improved, but we worry about correctness tradeoffs.
[01:05] Priya Nair: short answer: latency median dropped from ~220ms to ~140ms for the 256 context tests, p99 improved too, cost per 1k tokens about 28% lower, but on those 12 medical prompts the responses sometimes dropped an extra clarifying sentence or introduced a non-critical but incorrect suggestion.
[01:28] J. Kim: and to be explicit, our SLO is p95 < 300ms and model-level QA pass rate > 98% on the golden set, that 8% differential pushed some items under threshold.
[01:45] Alex Chen: thanks, so two levers: either widen pinning to a less aggressive quantized variant or keep v1.3 int8 but apply request-level soft-fallbacks for certain bucketed prompts; we should map which prompts need conservative routing.
[02:10] Renee: from privacy/compliance, we also need to make sure fallbacks don't route to a hosted model that persists logs differently — we prefer everything within the Dedicated tenant for PII traces.
[02:28] Liam O'Rourke: noted, we'll flag that. quick question—competitors? you mentioned vendor comparisons earlier, is there pressure to go with Anthropic or OpenAI?
[02:40] Marta Lopez: not pushing vendor swap, just benchmarking against them for cost/perf/context length. we need a safe plan to keep users up if we see degradations mid-rollout.
[02:55] Priya Nair: proposed technical plan: 1) pin default to v1.3-int8 for bulk traffic, 2) create prompt hash list (your golden 12 + failure examples) mapped to routing rule -> always go to v1.2-fp16, 3) implement a soft-escape route where model responses failing our QA heuristics are automatically replayed to fallback variant with request-id tagging.
[03:25] Samir Patel: replay sounds good, but how much latency will that add to tail? we can't double user facing latency.
[03:36] Priya Nair: we recommend async replay for non-blocking UX—serve the int8 answer, and for flagged items surface a follow-up correction when fallback returns, or run sync for admin channels. for critical flows we can configure sync fallback with a 300ms additional budget.
[03:58] Marta Lopez: for clinical notes we need synchronous guarantees, so we'll mark those prompt-hashes for sync fallback to fp16.
[04:12] Alex Chen: ok and rollbacks — we have an emergency cutover checklist: immediate rollback command to pin all routes to a safe baseline (v1.2 fp16), a fallback region plan, and circuit-breaker thresholds on error rate/QA fail rate > 2% over 5 min. we'll send that doc.
[04:33] J. Kim: how do we handle KV cache incompatibilities between versions during rollback? we saw earlier an issue where cache key formats changed.
[04:45] Priya Nair: good call—Priya: we recommend cold-start policy during rollback for first few minutes and version-aware cache keys; we'll include a back-compat shim in the runbook.
[05:00] Marta Lopez: can you also show the catalog metadata differences? we need to know exactly what changed (tokenizer tweaks, biases corrected, top_k defaults).
[05:12] Priya Nair: yes, Catalog diff summary: v1.3-int8 uses per-channel quantization, slightly different layernorm epsilon, and an updated tokenizer that merges some medical abbreviations. those tokenizer merges are likely the source of the omitted clarifying clause in a couple of examples.
[05:36] Alex Chen: action: Priya to produce a heatmap and catalog diff doc. Marta to provide the 12 prompts and 3 failure transcripts. Alex to send rollback runbook.
[05:50] Samir Patel: also want to run an experiment: mirror 10% production traffic to int8 and observe real-world metric delta for one day. can Redwood set that up in the sandbox?
[06:03] Liam O'Rourke: yes we can help configure traffic mirroring from Dedicated -> Canary pool; we'll need a network window and your ops okay.
[06:16] Renee: compliance asks: will mirrored traffic include PII? we need token redaction or synthetic dribble for mirrored samples.
[06:28] Priya Nair: we can redact at the routing layer or use anonymized payloads; we'll add a config flag.
[06:38] Alex Chen: ok circle back on the scheduling—practical items: benchmark run, golden prompt list, runbook email.
[06:47] [25:00] Priya Nair: jumping ahead to benchmarks—we ran an internal 1k request run earlier this morning to validate profiling, here's quick results: median latency v1.2 fp16: 210ms, v1.3 int8: 135ms; p99s were 780ms vs 540ms respectively, but the golden set QA pass dropped from 99.1% to 91.2% for int8 on long-context items. caveat: our internal seed set might not match your production distribution.
[07:25] Marta Lopez: 91.2% is worrying, can you break that down by prompt? which ones fail?
[07:36] Priya Nair: sure, failure bucket mostly on the three multi-step procedural prompts and one with nested conditionals; we'll send per prompt diffs.
[07:48] Samir Patel: what about cost numbers again? we need unit economics to evaluate:
[07:53] Priya Nair: approximate token cost delta: v1.2 fp16 $0.40 per 1k tokens, v1.3 int8 $0.29 per 1k tokens given current dedupe/caching. So about 27% savings.
[08:10] J. Kim: can we do model-level micro-traffic split on route level? for example, 95% to int8, 5% to fp16 for production for a week?
[08:22] Alex Chen: yes route-level hedging is supported; you can specify pin at route or prompt-hash granularity. It's also possible to have weighted variant routing for gradual ramp.
[08:35] Marta Lopez: one more ask—if we pin by prompt-hash does that block you from applying hotfixes? like small patching?
[08:44] Priya Nair: pinning is a routing rule, not a hard block; we can define an override channel for infra hotfixes so you can still push model patches with guardian approvals. We'll include that in the governance doc.
[08:58] Samir Patel: timeline wise, what do you recommend? keep int8 as default for next week and run mirror? or roll back to fp16 now?
[09:08] Alex Chen: suggested plan: keep int8 default in sandbox/stage; for production: enable 10% mirroring for 48 hours, run golden prompt checks daily; if QA pass for golden set stays > 97% and no new regressions, ramp to 50% then to 100% over a week. If at any point fail rate exceeds 2% over 5 minutes, auto-cutover to fp16 via circuit-breaker.
[09:35] Marta Lopez: sounds reasonable but we need the daily reporting and automated check, can Redwood surface that in Console?
[09:44] Liam O'Rourke: yes we can add a per-route QA monitor panel showing golden set pass rate, token cost, latency, and an alert on thresholds.
[09:55] Renee: also ensure audit logs capture who triggered overrides and any fallback events for SOC2 review.
[10:05] Priya Nair: absolutely, we'll enable request-level logging with masked PII and roll that into the audit stream for your Dedicated tenant.
[10:16] Alex Chen: wrapping up—recap of next steps and owners, and we'll send the benchmark artifacts and updated runbook.
[10:26] Marta Lopez: thanks, good progress.
[10:30] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and push the docs.

End of transcript.
